method: 26 of the 46 checks (Kitco spot, 23 listing pages, 2 Blue Nile policy pages) were re-opened live on 2026-10-25 with fetch_page and transcribed field by field into verification/evidence/3dfe4d85/ before any canonical value was touched. The remaining 20 checks — 2 Brilliant Earth listing reads whose USD price was not served today, 7 policy pages and 11 official references the fetch proxy failed for or that were not attempted after the outage began — are inherited unchanged from data/live_check_6d10ac0a.json (2026-10-23) with readBy labels naming the session that actually read them and an inheritedNote explaining the date. Two partial reads (BE-NADIA, BE-SECRET) and six failure records (F1–F6) are published below; nothing hidden by the outage is presented as read.
timeNote: Only the retrieval date is asserted for fetches. A time is recorded only where the source itself displayed one (Kitco's panel timestamp 'Oct 24, 2026 - 23:14 NY Time' and its body sentence 'as of October 24, 2026, 11:12 p.m. ET'). Etsy sale figures are relative countdowns captured at read time; no absolute expiry instant is recorded because none is published.
noHallucinations: Blank means unverified. A source conflict is published, not resolved by preference. Inherited reads keep their original dates, evidence ids and paths and are labelled with the session that actually made them. No EUR figure was converted to USD anywhere. Derived values are recomputed from the canonical inputs by script and re-checked by scripts/verify.py, scripts/independent_audit.py and tools/security_test.py.

checks.subject: 15 USC 297 identifying trademark
checks.sourceExcerpt: Official U.S. Government Publishing Office text; the link resolved to https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2024-title15/pdf/USCODE-2024-title15-chap8-sec297.pdf. '§ 297. Stamping plated articles'. (a) rolled gold plate / gold plate / gold filled / electroplate articles may not be stamped with any word or mark usually employed to indicate the fineness of gold 'unless such word or mark be accompanied by other words, plainly indicating that such article or part thereof is made of rolled gold plate, gold plate, or gold electroplate, or is gold filled, as the case may be'. (b) Identifying trademark: a manufacturer or dealer subject to section 294 who applies a quality mark indicating gold or silver content 'shall — (A) Apply or cause to be applied to that article a trademark of such persons, which has been duly registered or applied for registration under the laws of the United States ... or the name of such person', and each identifying trademark or name 'shall be applied to that article by the same means as that used in applying the quality mark or stamp appearing thereon, in type or lettering at least as large as that used in such quality mark or stamp, and in a position as close as possible to that quality mark or stamp.' (June 13, 1906, ch. 3289, § 4, 34 Stat. 261; Pub. L. 87-354, § 1, Oct. 4, 1961, 75 Stat. 775; Pub. L. 91-366, § 1(e), July 31, 1970, 84 Stat. 691.) scopeReads.subject: 16 CFR § 23.18 — Misrepresentation of weight and “total weight.”
scopeReads.sourceExcerpt: eCFR page state: 'This content is from the eCFR and is authoritative but unofficial. Displaying title 16, up to date as of 10/21/2026. Title 16 was last amended 10/19/2026.' Authority: 15 U.S.C. 45, 46. Source: 83 FR 40667, Aug. 16, 2018. Text: '(a) It is unfair or deceptive to misrepresent the weight of a diamond. (b) It is unfair or deceptive to use the word “point” or any abbreviation in any representation, advertising, marking, or labeling to describe the weight of a diamond, unless the weight is also stated as decimal parts of a carat (e.g., 25 points or .25 carat). A carat is a standard unit of weight for a diamond and is equivalent to 200 milligrams (1/5 gram). A point is one one-hundredth (1/100) of a carat.'
scopeReads.finding: § 23.18 governs DIAMOND weight representations. It does not require disclosure of a ring's gold-alloy gram weight, so the checklist no longer cites it as the basis for the grams criterion; it is cited for what it actually says, and the grams criterion is labelled as this project's buying rule.
